answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted attestation: every agent locks a slashable bond, and a new identity earns trust only after several already-bonded agents vouch for it. An attacker washing a river of fake accounts must post a fresh bond for each one, while every vouch must come from a distinct established account that forfeits its own stake if the fake is exposed. Trust becomes an island a single key cannot reach, and climbing each terrace of reputation means paying yet another bond plus bribes, so the cost grows faster than the number of sybils.
